BSBE 5100.title: Data-driven Cancer Research and Precision Medicine
BSBE 5100.description: This course covers emerging topics of big data analytics in cancer research. It will introduce the genetic basis of human cancer including mechanisms of mutations, mutation burden in cancer immunotherapy, integration of omics data, statistical method in differential gene expression, gene set enrichment analysis and so on. This course will also focus on the principles and applications of modern cancer therapeutic approaches and cutting-edge research in immunology. In addition, this course will discuss current practice of precision medicine and future developments.
cilos: Understand cancer immunotherapy, immunology, cancer stem cell, drug resistance and other oncology concepts.
Understand big data transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics and other omics used widely in cancer research.
Establish data analytics concepts in machine learning, statistical model, and neural network in the processing of high-throughput omics data.
Gain knowledge of current applications of precision medicine and future directions.
Utilize the statistical software R to perform differential gene expression and other big data analysis.

BSBE 5200.title: Principles of Neuroscience and Related Diseases
BSBE 5200.description: This course covers the basic knowledge of nervous system, and the clinical manifestation, anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of common nervous system diseases, with focus on the underlying molecular mechanism of the diseases and treatments.
cilos: Understand the basic anatomy and physiology of nervous system.
Attain basic knowledge in the manifestations, physiology, pathophysiology and treatment of common nervous system diseases.
Appreciate the molecular mechanism underlying common nervous system diseases and treatments.
Apply scientific knowledge and skills to interpret the pathogenesis of common nervous system diseases and evaluate the pros and cons of current treatments.

BSBE 5300.title: Brain and Behavior
BSBE 5300.description: This course covers the basic knowledge of neuroscience, including neuronal communications in the brain, the fundamental information and electrophysiological properties of neurons, neuroanatomy, psychopharmacology, and how the activity of neurons and neural circuits, together with chemical systems in the brains, yield emotion, motivated behaviors, learning and memory.
cilos: Acquire the basic knowledge of neural communication in the brain.
Explain the fundamental principles of chemical control of the brain.
Explain the fundamental principles of neural mechanisms of behaviors control.
Explain the neural mechanisms of learning and memory.
Apply and combine research methods and techniques to solve problems in neuroscience.

BSBE 5400.title: Fundamentals of Light Microscopy and Electronic Imaging
BSBE 5400.description: The goal of this course is to provide a fundamental introduction to light microscopy and electronic imaging. In the past 20 years, much has happened to light microscopy into the forefront of biomedical research methodologies. Topics to be covered include principles and practice of optical imaging, light and color, the point spread function and resolution, phase contrast microscopy and darkfield microscopy, differential interference contrast microscopy, fluorescence microscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, two-photon excitation fluorescence microscopy, super resolution imaging, imaging living cells with the microscope, digital imaging introduction and noise, digital image processing and other related topics.
cilos: Recognize the current research trend in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Understand the significance of light microscopy and electronic imaging, and emerging technologies in biological and physiological research.
Be acquainted with historical and current research based on bioimaging.
Choose the suitable microscope and imaging condition.
Process some advanced digital imaging pictures.
Review and present scientific literature through oral presentations.

BSBE 5500.title: Principles of Biomaterials, Drug Delivery and Tissue Engineering
BSBE 5500.description: This course covers the basic knowledge of biomaterials, drug delivery and tissue engineering: natural biomaterials, synthetic biomaterials, biomaterials for drug delivery, biomaterials for tissue engineering, biomaterial formulations (nanoparticles, nanofibers and microspheres), biocompatibility, biodegradability, with focus on the structure-function of the biomaterials and how to develop biomaterials for a variety of biomedical applications.
cilos: Have an overview of the basic concepts, functionalities, and applications of biomaterials.
Recognize the current research trend in biomaterials and understand the increasing significance of biomaterials and related applications.
Explain the theories and applications in biomaterials, drug delivery and tissue engineering.
Apply the methodologies and techniques to real problems in biomaterials and develop basic knowledge to conduct research in biomaterials.
Professionally present a research project, in the flow of introduction to the research question, the analysis method, solution approaches, outcomes and contributions.

BSBE 5600.title: Biosignal Processing
BSBE 5600.description: This course covers the principles, implementation and applications of signal processing methods in biological research and biomedical engineering. Through a series of case studies and projects, the course will provide opportunities to acquire practical knowledge and skills of data analysis. General concepts of signals and systems, and a brief tutorial of MATLAB will be introduced at the beginning. Then data acquisition, filtering, coding, feature extraction, statistical inference, pattern classification, and modeling will be covered with emphasis on applications in real-world data. This course also includes a topic about neural signal processing.

BSBE 5700.title: Medical Microrobotics: Principles and Applications
BSBE 5700.description: This course introduces microscopic robots and covers the fundamentals of their design, fabrication, and control for healthcare applications. Students will explore the interdisciplinary fields of engineering, materials science, medicine, and nanotechnology, and understand how these robots are set to revolutionize diagnostics, targeted therapy, and minimally invasive surgery. This course aims to equip students with the theoretical knowledge and practical insights necessary to contribute to this rapidly advancing field.
cilos: Understand the historical development and current state of medical microrobotics.

Strengthen the knowledge of fundamental principles of microrobotics, including scaling laws, fluid dynamics at micro and nano scales, and the challenges associated with low Reynolds number environments.
Understand the design, fabrication, and assembly processes of microrobots, incorporating knowledge of materials science and engineering at the micro and nano scales.
Understand the core technologies for microrobot control and navigation techniques.
Evaluate the design and application of biohybrid microrobots, understanding the integration of biological components with synthetic systems.
Gain knowledge on the application of microrobots in different medical scenarios and learn the cutting-edge technologies and theories from the recent research papers.
Understand the scientific and engineering challenges, recent advancements, and future directions in the field of medical microrobotics.
Cultivate cross-disciplinary capability, critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative research.

BSBE 5800.title: Concepts and Applications of Chemical Biology
BSBE 5800.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Chemical Biology, focusing on the concepts and development in applying chemical approaches to study and manipulate biological processes. Key topics include protein and nucleic acid chemistry, chemical genetics, bioorthogonal chemistry, and the design of chemical probesand reporters. Emphasis is placed on applying these tools to address challenging biological questions and drive drug discovery.
cilos: Describe the core principles and philosophy of chemical biology as an interdisciplinary field.
Explain the mechanistic basis and functional scope of key chemical biology methodologies.
Design experimental strategy that applies an appropriate chemical biology tool to investigate a specific biological question.
Present and evaluate the primary scientific literature in chemical biology.
Identify how chemical biology approaches enable discoveries and provide solutions.
Propose a research plan that integrates chemical biology concepts to address a challenge in fundamental science or clinical translation.

BSBE 5900.title: Introduction to Advanced Proteomics
BSBE 5900.description: Proteomics techniques are essential in biology and medicine for quantifying changes in protein levels and modifications, which are critical to understanding biological processes and disease. This course will introduce the fundamental theories and methodologies of proteomics, covering protein separation, identification, quantification, protein-protein interactions, and data analysis. Upon completion, students will possess a comprehensive understanding of how to apply proteomics techniques to solve complex problems in research and clinical settings.
cilos: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and applications of proteomics.
Explain the theoretical foundations and practical applications of proteomics in both research and clinical settings.
Apply proteomic methodologies to address specific research questions.
Acquire the fundamental knowledge required for data analysis in proteomics projects and adhere to ethical standards in scientific research.
Professionally present a research project.
Communicate and collaborate effectively within a team to complete a proteomics research project or assignment.

BSBE 6000.title: Special Topics in Bioscience
BSBE 6000.description: Selected topics in bioscience of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.
cilos: Identify the knowledge of the selected topics in the field of bioscience.

BSBE 6200.title: Independent Study
BSBE 6200.description: An independent research project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member on a Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering topic.
cilos: Demonstrate mastery of the knowledge and skills in the selected topics related to Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Apply an interdisciplinary approach in examining the selected topics.
Critically evaluate different aspects of the selected topics.
Communicate findings effectively in written reports.

BSBE 6800.title: Seminar in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering
BSBE 6800.description: Seminar topics presented by students, faculty and guest speakers. Students are expected to attend regularly and demonstrate proficiency in presentation in accordance with the program requirements. Graded P or F.
cilos: Demonstrate effective presentation skills in seminar presentations.
Understand current research trends and applications.
Engage argumentative and critical thinking skills.

BSBE 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
BSBE 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

BSBE 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
BSBE 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Bioscience and Biomedical Engineering.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
